original_test_intent: Verify that GPU events displayed by the BMC management interface use the same authoritative clock basis as the BMC Date and Time view, with a known timezone/offset, precision and acceptable skew, so GPU log chronology is trustworthy.
original_method: Select the unique row; identify BMC/SUT/GPU and firmware; record BMC timezone, UTC offset, NTP/synchronization status and clock precision without changing them; choose existing GPU events with stable IDs and known occurrence/retrieval times; capture their raw API/D-Bus timestamps and the BMC clock as closely together as possible; capture the same events and Date/Time view in WebUI; normalize values to UTC including offset and fractional precision; calculate per-event offset/skew and freshness under the approved oracle; retain empty/stale/API-GUI discrepancies without clearing or creating events.
manual_activity: An operator supplies the time semantics/tolerance and captures the BMC Web GPU Event Logs and Date/Time views; an agent can collect structured timestamps, normalize and compute skew.
required_inputs: BMC/SUT and exact GPU UUID/serial/slot/BDF plus firmware identities
Canonical GPU event-log API/D-Bus resource, stable record-ID mapping and corresponding WebUI row
Meaning of event timestamp and BMC time: UTC/local, offset/DST, precision, occurrence versus ingestion time
Approved maximum skew, freshness/sample selection, empty-log behavior and protected API/WebUI access
safety_requirements: Bind every compared event and clock value to the same BMC and GPU
Use only read-only time/event/API/UI operations and capture retrieval timestamps
Normalize timezone/offset and precision before comparing; do not compare rendered strings directly
Do not set clocks/NTP, inject GPU faults, clear logs or restart services
Stop on wrong target, ambiguous/stale/duplicate event, missing offset, API-GUI mismatch or excessive retrieval delay
agent_execution_scope: Collect complete raw BMC time and GPU event records from approved read-only resources
Resolve selected record IDs to the visible WebUI rows and normalize timestamps
Calculate skew according to the supplied occurrence/ingestion and tolerance rule
Do not create events, change time, clear logs, infer semantics from formatting or decide verdict
engineer_actions: Approve GPU-to-BMC record mapping and time-field semantics
Approve timezone/DST/precision normalization, sample freshness and skew tolerance
Approve empty/stale-log handling and GUI/API equivalence
Review measured discrepancies and decide PASS, FAIL, or BLOCKED

command_applicability.original_deepseek_command_fit: The proposed Redfish/D-Bus read plus WebUI cross-check matches the source, but no concrete resource or event identity is supplied and 'match' requires time-base and tolerance definitions.
command_applicability.command_recommendation: Query approved BMC clock and GPU log resources in one bounded interval, record retrieval times, normalize selected stable event IDs to UTC, compute skew and capture the same rows plus Date/Time page in WebUI.
command_applicability.original_parameters_and_time_preserved: BMC Web GPU Event Logs, BMC Date and Time, timestamp matching, Common scope and 5/5-minute estimate remain.

modernized_recommendation.recommended_method: Use stable event IDs and dual raw/rendered evidence to distinguish source-event time, BMC ingestion time and current clock, then normalize all values before a tolerance-based comparison.
modernized_recommendation.difference_from_original_method: Adds GPU identity, record mapping, time-field semantics, UTC/offset normalization, retrieval timing, explicit skew and stale-data handling.
modernized_recommendation.coverage_difference: Visually similar minute-level strings can conceal timezone or seconds-level drift, while comparing an old event timestamp directly to the current BMC clock would be logically invalid.
modernized_recommendation.risks_limitations: GPU events may be generated in GPU firmware time and converted when ingested by BMC; without vendor semantics the displayed field might not be expected to equal current time, only the event's occurrence time on a synchronized base.

project_override_considerations: If no safe existing GPU event is fresh enough, engineering should provide a benign vendor-approved event stimulus as a separate authorized prerequisite; the review must not invent or inject a GPU fault. A WebUI-local timezone transformation is acceptable only when its rule is documented and API values reconcile after normalization.
expected_evidence: BMC timezone/offset/DST/NTP status, current-time raw value and retrieval timestamp
Complete selected GPU event raw records, stable IDs, event-time semantics and retrieval timestamps
WebUI GPU-event and Date/Time screenshots mapped to the same values
Normalized UTC values, per-event skew/tolerance/freshness calculation and API-GUI reconciliation
No-clock/log mutation audit and engineer verdict

source_conflict_analysis.analysis: Items, Procedure and Criteria consistently require GPU event timestamps and BMC time to be compared in BMC Web. The exact semantics and tolerance are missing but not contradictory.

blocked_analysis.analysis: The read-only comparison and GUI surfaces are identifiable. Vendor time semantics, event mapping and tolerance are supplyable project inputs, so the case remains executable with confirmation.

engineering_decision_pending.question: Resolve Functionality row 2238 Wistron-BMC Sanity-00020-V001: approve the BMC/SUT/GPU UUID/serial/slot/BDF and firmware mapping; canonical GPU event API/D-Bus resource plus stable record-ID-to-WebUI mapping; whether each timestamp is GPU occurrence or BMC ingestion time, UTC/local/DST/offset and precision; sample freshness/empty-log behavior, maximum skew/retrieval delay, API-GUI reconciliation and safe non-mutating evidence path.

review_improvement: Preserves the BMC Web comparison while preventing formatted strings, old events or mismatched GPU records from being mistaken for proof of clock synchronization.
independent_technical_reasoning: An event log timestamp is historical, so it should not numerically equal the current BMC clock unless acquisition is tied to event creation. The real invariant is that event occurrence/ingestion uses the same synchronized time base within a documented skew. The WebUI may convert UTC for display, and API precision may exceed what is shown, making normalization and stable record mapping essential. Because the source explicitly names WebUI surfaces, structured API evidence improves but cannot eliminate the operator visual cross-check.
